answer: Latency triangulation makes clone farms visible. Each epoch, five random peers in different regions ping every key and record round-trip times. Keys on one machine return near-identical timing profiles, the same pigment in every stroke, so the protocol groups them and splits a single reward across the group. Faking distinct profiles means renting real servers on separate networks, a cost that flows like a river with every extra key, while an honest agent on its own mesa pays nothing extra.
